# NeuralNg

For one provider that owns primary and surface palettes, color mode, direction,
DOM attributes, persistence, and cross-tab synchronization, import
provideNeuralAppearance and NeuralAppearanceService from
@neural-ng/core/appearance. Do not register provideNeuralColorMode beside
provideNeuralAppearance; Appearance already configures the color-mode
controller. Read its Signal properties and call setPrimary, setSurface,
setMode, or setDirection; do not mutate NeuralNg CSS variables directly.
Custom palette names must be registered through the provider before use.

> NeuralNg is an AI-first, headless Angular 22+ UI component library using standalone components, Signals, strict TypeScript, native accessibility semantics, SSR-safe code, and secondary package entry points.

For machine-readable discovery, run `npx -y @neural-ng/mcp-server`. The MCP
server is read-only and exposes exact component contracts, package exports,
themes, README files, and llms.txt resources. Use its returned entry points,
selectors, and models without inventing aliases.

Generate only modern Angular code. Import each component from its exact secondary
entry point. Do not create consumer NgModules. Prefer visible labels, native HTML
semantics, and documented signal inputs and outputs. Import a theme explicitly
unless every used component is unstyled.

Use `provideNeuralNg({ unstyled, direction, density })` for application-wide
configuration. `direction: 'auto'` follows the active NeuralNg locale. Use
`NeuralNgService.setDirection(...)` and `setDensity(...)` for runtime changes.
A component-level unstyled input remains valid for local control.

Import localization APIs from `@neural-ng/core/i18n` and locale data from exact
tree-shakable entry points. Official complete packs are `en`, `tr`, `de`, `fr`,
`es`, `pt-br`, `ar`, and `zh-cn`. Set an explicit
initial locale with `provideNeuralNg({ locale })`; use
`NeuralLocaleService.use(locale)` for runtime switching. Do not infer
`navigator.language` during component rendering.

Neural Icons is an optional separate package. Import
`@neural-ng/icons/icons.css` once and use `class="nt nt-{name}"`. Core
components must not assume that Neural Icons is installed.

Import `NeuralButton` from `@neural-ng/core/button`. Use `size` for the complete
control and `iconSize="small|medium|large"` only when the glyph needs an
independent override. When `iconSize` is omitted, it follows the Button size.

Import Accordion from `@neural-ng/core/accordion`. Prefer `items` for plain
text data and projected panel/header/content composition for custom Angular
markup. Bind `[(value)]`; add `multiple` for array state. Never combine both
content sources.

Import AutoComplete from `@neural-ng/core/auto-complete`. Bind `[(value)]` for
the committed form value and `[(query)]` for editable text. Use local mode for
deterministic client filtering and `dataMode="remote"` with `(search)` for API
results; ignore stale responses using `requestId`. IME composition must not
emit partial searches. Keep DOM focus on the combobox input and preserve its
`aria-activedescendant` listbox model. The shared Popover already uses the
browser top layer and matches the input width; do not add appendTo logic.

Import `NeuralBreadcrumb` from `@neural-ng/core/breadcrumb`. Prefer `routerLink`
plus Angular Router options for SPA navigation and `href` for native links.
Use `maxItems` for Menu-backed overflow; RouterLink behavior is preserved for
overflowed items. Let the last item represent the current page unless `current`
is explicit.

Import `NeuralCard`, `NeuralCardHeader`, `NeuralCardBody`, and
`NeuralCardFooter` from `@neural-ng/core/card`. Project real headings, media,
content, and interactive components; Card intentionally owns only the semantic
surface and section composition. Never generate the deprecated `CardComponent`
family of aliases.

Import `NeuralCheckbox` and `NeuralTriStateCheckbox` from
`@neural-ng/core/checkbox`. Keep binary `checked: boolean` separate from
tri-state `value: boolean | null`; never invent a nullable binary model or a
second indeterminate source. Do not generate the deprecated
`CheckboxComponent` aliases.

Import `NeuralConfirmDialog` and `NeuralConfirmationService` from
`@neural-ng/core/confirm-dialog`. Render a host for each key and open it through
the service. Async actions may return false to keep the dialog open. The latest
same-key request replaces the active request; never invent queue behavior or
generate the deprecated `ConfirmDialogComponent` alias.

Import Badge from `@neural-ng/core/badge`. Use `max` for numeric visual caps,
add `ariaLabel` to meaningful dot badges, and use `ariaLive` only for relevant
dynamic updates. Zero and negative values are not empty.

Import Avatar from `@neural-ng/core/avatar`. Prefer `name` for accessible
initials fallback, compose status through `NeuralBadgeDirective`, and use
AvatarGroup `max` for localized +N overflow.

Import Tag from `@neural-ng/core/tag`. Use it for textual classification or
status, not compact counts. `removed` is controlled: update the owning
collection after receiving `{ value, originalEvent }`.

Keep theme identity and color mode independent. Use `data-neural-theme` for the
theme family and `data-neural-mode="light|dark"` for the resolved mode. Import
the optional Signal controller from `@neural-ng/core/color-mode`; never assume
Tailwind or mutate its generic `.dark` class.

The stable primitive palettes are `--neural-color-primary-{50..950}` and
`--neural-color-surface-{50..950}`, plus `--neural-color-surface-0`. Primitive
steps do not reverse in dark mode; semantic aliases choose accessible steps.
For Tailwind CSS v4, import `@neural-ng/core/themes/tailwind.css` after
`tailwindcss` to generate `primary-*` and `surface-*` color utilities. Do not
add Tailwind as a NeuralNg runtime dependency.

Import pagination from `@neural-ng/core/paginator`. It uses zero-based
`pageIndex` and `pageSize` model inputs, emits slice-compatible `startIndex`
and exclusive `endIndex`, and includes a polite range report by default.

Import canonical `NeuralDatePicker` from `@neural-ng/core/date-picker`.
`DatePickerComponent` is a deprecated compatibility alias. Its models are immutable,
timezone-safe `NeuralDateParts`, `NeuralTimeParts`, and
`NeuralDateTimeParts` objects. Use `pickerMode="time"` for time only and
`pickerMode="datetime"` for calendar plus time. Time modes always keep edits in
an Apply/Cancel draft. Configure 12/24-hour display with `hourFormat`, optional
seconds with `showSeconds`, increments with `hourStep`, `minuteStep`, and
`secondStep`, and datetime bounds with `minDateTime`/`maxDateTime`. Do not bind
JavaScript Date objects or parse locale-formatted display strings as models.
Use `formatNeuralLocaleDate` for display and `parseNeuralLocaleDate` for strict
locale text parsing. The parser returns null for wrong field order, wrong
separators, impossible Gregorian dates, or unsupported text; never use
`Date.parse`. Preserve the built-in dialog/grid semantics, roving tabindex,
polite view announcement, full accessible weekday names, and RTL-aware physical
Left/Right movement.
DatePicker supports local `unstyled`, global `provideNeuralNg({ unstyled:
true })`, and `NeuralDatePickerClasses`. Keep structural `*-root` hooks and ARIA
behavior; remove only visual `*-base` classes. Apply customization in this
order: structural hooks, component tokens, active theme tokens, consumer
classes. Neutral owns the stable DatePicker tokens; Glass and Futuristic are
token-only overrides. For custom content import and use the typed standalone
directives `NeuralDatePickerDayTemplate`, `NeuralDatePickerHeaderTemplate`,
`NeuralDatePickerFooterTemplate`, `NeuralDatePickerTriggerIconTemplate`,
`NeuralDatePickerPreviousIconTemplate`, and
`NeuralDatePickerNextIconTemplate`; do not replace internal keyboard or overlay
logic.
DatePicker implements `FormValueControl<NeuralDatePickerValue<...>>`. Bind it
with `[formField]` for Signal Forms, `[formControl]` for Reactive Forms, or
`[(ngModel)]` for template-driven forms. Do not add a ControlValueAccessor or a
second value store. Preserve `touch` emission on composite blur/close and allow
the form to own touched, dirty, disabled, readonly, required, and invalid state.
Use semantic outputs `opened`, `closed`, `selected`, `cleared`, `viewChanged`,
`monthChanged`, `yearChanged`, and `invalidInput`; use `valueChange` only for
plain model synchronization.
DatePicker needs no `appendTo="body"`: its Popover uses the browser top layer,
retains Angular DOM ownership, restores focus for explicit closes, and releases
all overlay positioning resources on destroy. It renders closed during SSR.

Import ProgressBar from `@neural-ng/core/progress-bar`. Use determinate mode
for known numeric progress and mode="indeterminate" when completion is unknown.
Provide ariaLabel or ariaLabelledBy, use ariaValueText for localized
descriptions, and never expose numeric ARIA values for indeterminate progress.

Import ProgressSpinner from `@neural-ng/core/progress-spinner`. It is always
indeterminate and receives a localized default accessible name. Use it for
compact unknown-duration tasks and use ProgressBar for numeric progress.

Import canonical `NeuralLoadingOverlay` from `@neural-ng/core/loading-overlay`.
`LoadingOverlayComponent` is a deprecated compatibility alias. It composes
ProgressSpinner while owning container/viewport blocking, aria-busy, timing,
focus restoration, and scroll locking. Use neuralLoadingIndicator for custom
visuals without reimplementing loading behavior.

Import Skeleton from `@neural-ng/core/skeleton`. It is decorative and always
aria-hidden. Put aria-busy on the surrounding loading region; use LoadingOverlay
when interaction must be blocked. Prefer wave for active fetching, pulse for
calm placeholders, and none when motion is unnecessary.

Import MeterGroup from `@neural-ng/core/meter-group`. Use it for multiple
scalar measurements inside a known range, never loading progress. Every item
must have a meaningful label and numeric value; use valueText for human-friendly
assistive descriptions and valueFormatter only for visible text.

Import Table from `@neural-ng/core/table`. Preserve its native table semantics,
provide `rowKey` for stable selection and expansion. Client selection supports
row click, Ctrl/Meta toggles, Shift ranges, keyboard navigation, disabled rows,
and page/filtered/all select-all scopes. Remote selection is key-only through
`selectionKeys`; use `dataMode="remote"` when the server owns sorting,
filtering, paging, or selection identity. Use
`editMode="cell"` or `"row"` with typed `neuralTableEditor` templates for
immutable editing. Table never mutates supplied rows; apply `draftRow` from
`cellEditComplete` or `rowEditSave`. `editValidator` supports synchronous or
Promise validation, while `readOnly` locks individual cells. Use
`scrollHeight` with `stickyHeader`, `[(columnWidths)]` with
`resizableColumns`, and `[(hiddenColumnIds)]` for controlled column layout.

Import composable cards from `@neural-ng/core/card`. Use `neural-card` with
optional header/body/footer components, native headings, and `ariaLabelledby`
when an accessible name is needed.

Import `NeuralDialog`, `NeuralDialogHeader`, `NeuralDialogBody`,
`NeuralDialogFooter`, and `NeuralDialogInitialFocus` from
`@neural-ng/core/dialog`; never generate their deprecated `Dialog*` aliases.
It renders native `<dialog>` and uses an `open` model. Compose
header/body/footer, provide `ariaLabelledby` or
`ariaLabel`, and prefer `neuralDialogInitialFocus` on the first meaningful
control. Use the optional `closed` event only when its close reason is needed.
Set `showFullScreenButton` for the localized maximize/minimize action and bind
`fullChange` only when application state must observe user toggles.

Import `NeuralDrawer`, `NeuralDrawerHeader`, `NeuralDrawerBody`,
`NeuralDrawerFooter`, and `NeuralDrawerInitialFocus` from
`@neural-ng/core/drawer`; never generate their deprecated `Drawer*` aliases.
Use logical start/end positions, a visible accessible heading, and native
modal focus behavior.

Import `NeuralDivider` from `@neural-ng/core/divider`. Use it for semantic content
boundaries, choose horizontal or vertical orientation, and prefer label for
plain text or projection for richer markup. Do not use Divider only to create
layout spacing.

Import Checkbox controls from `@neural-ng/core/checkbox`. Use
`neural-checkbox` with a boolean `checked` model for binary fields. Use
`neural-tri-state-checkbox` with a `boolean | null` `value` model when mixed
state is required. Both work with Signal Forms, Reactive Forms, and ngModel.
Use `stateChange` for detailed user events; programmatic writes must not emit it.

Import RadioGroup and Radio from `@neural-ng/core/radio`. RadioGroup implements
`FormValueControl<TValue | null>` and works with `[formField]`, `[formControl]`,
and `[(ngModel)]`. Use `selectionChange` only for pointer or keyboard selection;
programmatic writes must not emit it. Readonly groups remain focusable and
expose `aria-readonly` without disabling native radio inputs. Radio is an option
inside RadioGroup, not an independent form control.

Import Input from `@neural-ng/core/input` and apply it as
`<input neuralInput>`. The host stays native, so use native labels, attributes,
classes, events, and Angular `[formField]`; never generate `<neural-input>`.
For logical start/end icons, also import `NeuralInputGroup` and project the
native input inside `<neural-input-group startIcon="nt nt-search">`.

Import canonical `NeuralInputMask` from `@neural-ng/core/input-mask`.
`InputMaskComponent` is a deprecated compatibility alias. Bind the string model
through `[(value)]`, `[formField]`, `[formControl]`, or `[(ngModel)]`. Mask rule
`9` accepts an ASCII digit, `a` accepts a Unicode letter, and `*` accepts a
Unicode letter or number. Use `unmask` only when the application contract wants
raw slot characters; masking is not a substitute for server validation.

Import canonical `NeuralInputNumber` from `@neural-ng/core/input-number`.
`InputNumberComponent` is a deprecated compatibility alias. Bind `[(value)]` as
`number | null`, never as formatted text. Use `mode="currency"` with an ISO
currency code, and allow the locale service to own parsing and formatting.
`valueCommit` is optional; normal binding never requires an event type import.

Import canonical `NeuralInputOtp` from `@neural-ng/core/input-otp`.
`InputOtpComponent` is a deprecated compatibility alias. Bind the entire code as
one string through `[(value)]` or an Angular Forms adapter. Use native
`autocomplete="one-time-code"`; verification, expiry and retry policy always
belong on the server.

Import FileUpload from `@neural-ng/core/file-upload`. Bind a
`readonly File[]` model in every mode. FileUpload owns native choose, drag and
drop, client-side validation, removal, and clearing; it never performs HTTP
requests. Build `FormData` in application code, never JSON-stringify File
objects, and repeat type, size, filename, and content validation on the server.
Use `selectionChange` for accepted plus rejected details. `accept`,
`maxFileSize`, `maxFiles`, and duplicate checks are UX constraints only.

Install Editor with `npm install @neural-ng/editor` and import canonical
`NeuralEditor` from `@neural-ng/editor`. `EditorComponent` is a deprecated
compatibility alias. The Editor package owns its Tiptap, ProseMirror, Floating
UI, and Yjs runtime dependencies, so applications must not install or import
those internals directly. Bind only a `NeuralEditorDocument` JSON value; never
bind HTML, Markdown, or a format union. Use `NeuralEditorController`, stable
node IDs, typed operations, provider-neutral AI proposals, and explicit
collaboration providers. Editor never saves, uploads, invokes AI, opens network
connections, or sanitizes backend output.


Import `NeuralField`, `NeuralFieldLabel`, `NeuralFieldHint`,
`NeuralFieldError`, and `NeuralFieldControl` from `@neural-ng/core/field`.
Never generate their deprecated `FieldComponent` or `Field*Directive` aliases.
Use a required, deterministic `controlId`, `<label neuralFieldLabel>`,
hint/error directives, and either `neuralInput` or `neuralFieldControl`. Keep
validation in the form schema; Field only synchronizes accessible relationships
and presentation state.

Import composable tabs from `@neural-ng/core/tabs`. Match each tab value to a
panel value, label every tab list, and use the `value` model input. A tab accepts
either projected icon markup or the concise `iconClass` input.
Horizontal lists provide native overflow scrolling; styled tabs include
reduced-motion-aware indicator and panel-enter feedback.

Import Select from `@neural-ng/core/select`. Select implements
`FormValueControl<TValue | null>` and supports `[formField]`, `[formControl]`,
`[(ngModel)]`, or plain `[(value)]`. Prefer `[options]` with `optionLabel` and
`optionValue` for object arrays. Use projected `neural-option` declarations as
an alternative for custom content, never as a second source in the same Select.
Use `selectionChange` only for pointer or keyboard value changes; programmatic
writes must not emit it. Readonly remains focusable, exposes `aria-readonly`,
and blocks pointer, keyboard, and clear mutation. Use `cleared` and
`openChange`; do not invent `onSelected`, `onChange`, or `onSelectLink`.

Import canonical `NeuralMultiSelect` from `@neural-ng/core/multi-select`; never
generate the deprecated `MultiSelectComponent` alias. Its `value` model is
always an immutable readonly array. Prefer data-driven options with optionLabel/optionValue,
`display="chip"` for removable values, and `selectionChange` as the main event.
The popup matches the trigger width and supports local or request-ID based
remote filtering. Keep unstyled structural hooks and typed class slots intact.
Build dependent selects from Signals and reset the child value when its parent
selection changes.

Import TreeSelect from `@neural-ng/core/tree-select`. Map immutable nested
options with `optionLabel`, `optionValue`, and `optionChildren`. Single mode
writes a scalar or null; multiple and checkbox modes write immutable arrays.
Use `optionKey` when `optionValue` resolves to an object. TreeSelect composes
Tree keyboard/selection behavior with the top-layer Popover foundation; never
recreate either controller in application code.

Import `NeuralDataView` from `@neural-ng/core/data-view`; never generate the
deprecated `DataViewComponent` alias. Keep it presentation-only:
compose actions, selection, and editing inside typed item templates instead of
adding them to DataView state. Bind the source collection to the template
directive (`[neuralDataViewListItem]="products"` or
`[neuralDataViewGridItem]="products"`) so Angular infers the item type. Local
mode owns stable nested-field sorting and paging. Remote mode must receive the
current server page through `value`, the full count through `totalRecords`, and
must load from the serializable `stateChange` or `pageChange` event. Use the
separate VirtualScroller entry point when windowing is required.

Import `NeuralVirtualScroller` from `@neural-ng/core/virtual-scroller`. Provide fixed,
positive `itemSize` and `viewportSize` values and bind the collection to the
typed item template directive. Treat every range end as exclusive. Use
`rangeChange` for client observation and `lazyLoad` for remote range requests.
Do not put selection, editing, tree state, or variable-height measurement into
the VirtualScroller contract.

Import RadioGroup and Radio from `@neural-ng/core/radio`. Prefer `[options]`
with `optionLabel` and `optionValue` for data-driven groups; use projected
`neural-radio` children as an alternative for rich content. Bind `[(value)]`
and use `selectionChange` for detailed user-only events. Do not combine both
option sources or invent a toggle-to-null behavior.

Import Switch from `@neural-ng/core/switch`. It implements
`FormCheckboxControl` with one strict boolean `checked` model. Bind with
`[formField]`, `[formControl]`, `[(ngModel)]`, or plain `[(checked)]`, and
project a visible label. Programmatic writes must not emit `stateChange`; one
user change emits one detailed event, and `touch` emits on native blur. Switch
is never tri-state; use `neural-tri-state-checkbox` when null/mixed is part of
the domain. Readonly stays focusable but cannot be changed.

Import Textarea from `@neural-ng/core/textarea` and generate
`<textarea neuralTextarea>`, never a custom textarea element. Keep native
attributes and events on that host and bind Signal Forms directly. `autoResize`
uses CSS `field-sizing: content`; `resizeMode` controls manual resizing.

Import NeuralTooltip from `@neural-ng/core/tooltip` and apply
`neuralTooltip="Plain descriptive text"` to the trigger. Tooltip is text-only,
opens on hover and focus, and closes on leave, blur, or Escape. Use
`tooltipPosition`, delays, typed class slots, and `unstyled` only when needed.
Never put interactive content in a tooltip.

Import canonical `NeuralPanelMenu` from `@neural-ng/core/panel-menu`. It is an inline
Accordion + Tree hierarchy, not a Sidebar and not a popup Menu. Use unique
stable item keys, bind `[(expandedKeys)]`, emit leaf actions through
`itemSelect`, and use `itemToggle` only when branch details are needed. Never
generate a trigger button or Overlay integration for PanelMenu. Use `href` for
native links and `routerLink` plus Angular Router options for SPA navigation.

Import canonical `NeuralMenu` from `@neural-ng/core/menu`. It is a flat command list. Use
`[neuralMenuTriggerFor]` only with `<neural-menu popup>`; inline Menu needs no
trigger. Emit actions through `itemSelect`. Do not generate nested Menu items;
use PanelMenu for inline hierarchy and reserve popup nesting for TieredMenu.
Use `routerLink` plus Angular Router options for SPA navigation and `href` for
native or external navigation.

Import `NeuralSidebar`, `NeuralSidebarLayout`, the header/content/footer
primitives, `NeuralSidebarMain`, and `NeuralSidebarTrigger` from
`@neural-ng/core/sidebar`. Sidebar owns application-shell layout and responsive
collapse state; it does not own navigation entries. Compose NeuralMenu or
NeuralPanelMenu inside NeuralSidebarContent. Use Drawer for transient arbitrary
tasks instead of persistent application navigation. Bind `[(open)]`, give the
Sidebar a stable `id`, and connect a native button or NeuralButton with
`[neuralSidebarTrigger]="'id'"`. Use logical `side="start|end"`. Desktop defaults
to icon collapse and mobile to offcanvas at `breakpoint="64rem"`. Preserve
accessible naming, Escape/backdrop dismissal, focus restoration, structural
hooks, and unstyled class ownership.

Import Popover from `@neural-ng/core/popover`. Apply
`[neuralPopoverTriggerFor]="panel"` to a native interactive trigger and place
arbitrary Angular content in `<neural-popover #panel>`. Prefer logical
`bottom-start` or `bottom-end` placement. Popover is non-modal, does not trap
focus, and needs no `appendTo="body"` because it uses the browser top layer.
Use `neuralPopoverClose` for in-panel dismissal and
`neuralPopoverInitialFocus` only with an explicit first-focus workflow. Use
Dialog for modal content and Menu for command-list semantics.

## Components

- [Accordion documentation](./accordion/README.md): Data and projected panels, Signals state, keyboard behavior, typed class slots, tokens, and beta boundaries.
- [Accordion AI context](./accordion/llms.txt): Deterministic Accordion generation rules and canonical composition.
- [AutoComplete documentation](./auto-complete/README.md): Local and remote suggestions, dual Signal models, Forms, templates, accessibility, and headless slots.
- [AutoComplete AI context](./auto-complete/llms.txt): Deterministic editable combobox generation and request-race rules.
- [MultiSelect documentation](./multi-select/README.md): Chips, filtering, grouped options, Forms, accessibility, and headless slots.
- [MultiSelect AI context](./multi-select/llms.txt): Deterministic multiple-selection generation rules.
- [TreeSelect documentation](./tree-select/README.md): Hierarchical option mapping, selection modes, Forms, Popover composition, and headless slots.
- [TreeSelect AI context](./tree-select/llms.txt): Deterministic hierarchical-picker generation rules.
- [DataView documentation](./data-view/README.md): Typed list/grid presentation, local and remote state, Paginator composition, and headless slots.
- [DataView AI context](./data-view/llms.txt): Deterministic collection-presentation and remote-state rules.
- [VirtualScroller documentation](./virtual-scroller/README.md): Fixed-size vertical/horizontal windowing, lazy ranges, programmatic scrolling, and headless slots.
- [VirtualScroller AI context](./virtual-scroller/llms.txt): Deterministic range and composition rules.
- [Breadcrumb documentation](./breadcrumb/README.md): Router links, projected items, responsive Menu overflow, semantics, and headless slots.
- [Breadcrumb AI context](./breadcrumb/llms.txt): Deterministic breadcrumb generation rules.
- [Badge documentation](./badge/README.md): Counts, caps, semantic states, dots, projected content, and headless slots.
- [Badge AI context](./badge/llms.txt): Deterministic Badge generation and accessibility rules.
- [Avatar documentation](./avatar/README.md): Images, initials, icon and projected fallbacks, Badge composition, groups, and headless slots.
- [Avatar AI context](./avatar/llms.txt): Deterministic Avatar fallback, accessibility, Badge, and grouping rules.
- [ProgressBar documentation](./progress-bar/README.md): Determinate, buffered, and indeterminate progress, accessibility, motion, tokens, and headless slots.
- [ProgressBar AI context](./progress-bar/llms.txt): Deterministic ProgressBar generation and accessibility rules.
- [ProgressSpinner documentation](./progress-spinner/README.md): SVG indeterminate progress, localization, motion, styling, and headless slots.
- [ProgressSpinner AI context](./progress-spinner/llms.txt): Deterministic ProgressSpinner generation and accessibility rules.
- [LoadingOverlay documentation](./loading-overlay/README.md): Container and viewport blocking, timing, focus, scroll, custom indicators, and headless slots.
- [LoadingOverlay AI context](./loading-overlay/llms.txt): Deterministic blocking-loader generation and composition rules.
- [Skeleton documentation](./skeleton/README.md): Decorative placeholders, CSS sizing, shapes, motion, accessibility, and headless slots.
- [Skeleton AI context](./skeleton/llms.txt): Deterministic Skeleton generation and accessibility rules.
- [MeterGroup documentation](./meter-group/README.md): Multiple scalar meters, ranges, layouts, labels, colors, icons, and headless slots.
- [MeterGroup AI context](./meter-group/llms.txt): Deterministic MeterGroup generation and accessibility rules.
- [Table documentation](./table/README.md): Native data table, client and remote state, filters, advanced selection, immutable cell/row editing, expansion, resize, visibility, controlled column ordering, grouped headers, summaries, localization, and headless slots.
- [Table AI context](./table/llms.txt): Deterministic Table generation, data-mode, column layout, ordering, grouped headers, summaries, and accessibility rules.
- [NeuralButton documentation](./button/README.md): Public API, examples, styling contract, accessibility, and SSR behavior.
- [NeuralButton AI context](./button/llms.txt): Concise generation rules and canonical NeuralButton example.
- [Tag documentation](./tag/README.md): Text labels, semantic states, icons, controlled removal, and headless slots.
- [Tag AI context](./tag/llms.txt): Deterministic Tag selection and generation rules.
- [Card documentation](./card/README.md): Composable native sections, typed class slots, tokens, accessibility, and unstyled usage.
- [Card AI context](./card/llms.txt): Deterministic Card composition rules and canonical example.
- [Dialog documentation](./dialog/README.md): Native modal behavior, focus, close reasons, composition, class slots, tokens, and SSR.
- [Dialog AI context](./dialog/llms.txt): Deterministic native Dialog generation rules and canonical composition.
- [Divider documentation](./divider/README.md): Semantic orientation, labels, projected content, line variants, and headless slots.
- [Divider AI context](./divider/llms.txt): Deterministic Divider generation and accessibility rules.
- [Checkbox documentation](./checkbox/README.md): Native binary and tri-state behavior, events, Field composition, classes, and tokens.
- [Checkbox AI context](./checkbox/llms.txt): Deterministic Checkbox generation rules and tri-state contract.
- [Input documentation](./input/README.md): Native host, forms, accessibility, class ownership, states, and tokens.
- [Input AI context](./input/llms.txt): Deterministic native Input generation rules and canonical Signal Forms example.
- [InputMask documentation](./input-mask/README.md): Canonical component, deterministic mask grammar, caret-aware editing, Forms, accessibility, and headless classes.
- [InputMask AI context](./input-mask/llms.txt): Deterministic masked-input generation rules.
- [InputNumber documentation](./input-number/README.md): Localized parsing, currency, bounds, Signal Forms, accessibility, and headless classes.
- [InputNumber AI context](./input-number/llms.txt): Deterministic numeric-control generation rules.
- [InputOtp documentation](./input-otp/README.md): Autofill, paste, Forms, keyboard, accessibility, security boundaries, and headless classes.
- [InputOtp AI context](./input-otp/llms.txt): Deterministic one-time-code generation rules.
- [FileUpload documentation](./file-upload/README.md): Canonical
  `NeuralFileUpload`, immutable file arrays, drag and drop, client-side
  rejection events, Forms, and HTTP ownership boundaries.
- [FileUpload AI context](./file-upload/llms.txt): Deterministic file-selection generation rules and FormData guidance.
- [Editor documentation](./editor/README.md): Structured JSON values, Tiptap integration, controller commands, Forms, serializers, security, and headless slots.
- [Editor AI context](./editor/llms.txt): Deterministic rich-text generation rules and application ownership boundaries.
- [Field documentation](./field/README.md): Labels, descriptions, validation presentation, native control bridge, state, tokens, and unstyled usage.
- [Field AI context](./field/llms.txt): Deterministic Field composition and Signal Forms generation rules.
- [Radio documentation](./radio/README.md): Data and projected choices, native semantics, keyboard behavior, Field composition, classes, and tokens.
- [Radio AI context](./radio/llms.txt): Deterministic RadioGroup generation rules and canonical examples.
- [Select documentation](./select/README.md): Data and projected options, events, keyboard behavior, chained selects, classes, and tokens.
- [Select AI context](./select/llms.txt): Deterministic Select generation rules and canonical data-driven example.
- [Switch documentation](./switch/README.md): Native switch semantics, boolean state, readonly behavior, Field composition, classes, and tokens.
- [Switch AI context](./switch/llms.txt): Deterministic Switch generation rules and canonical example.
- [Textarea documentation](./textarea/README.md): Native host, Signal Forms, auto resize, resize modes, Field composition, states, classes, and tokens.
- [Textarea AI context](./textarea/llms.txt): Deterministic native Textarea generation rules and canonical example.
- [Toast documentation](./toast/README.md): v0.1 providers, nine positions, modern animation, templates, progress, swipe, accessibility, class hooks, and unstyled usage.
- [Toast AI context](./toast/llms.txt): Deterministic generation rules and canonical Toast example.
- [Tabs documentation](./tabs/README.md): Composition, icon options, keyboard behavior, class slots, tokens, and SSR-safe IDs.
- [Tabs AI context](./tabs/llms.txt): Deterministic Tabs generation rules and canonical example.
- [Tooltip documentation](./tooltip/README.md): Positions, delays, accessibility, class slots, and disabled-control guidance.
- [Tooltip AI context](./tooltip/llms.txt): Deterministic Tooltip generation rules.
- [PanelMenu documentation](./panel-menu/README.md): Recursive data, projected items, Signals expansion, keyboard behavior, and headless slots.
- [PanelMenu AI context](./panel-menu/llms.txt): Deterministic inline hierarchy generation rules.
- [Sidebar documentation](./sidebar/README.md): Application shell, responsive collapse, logical placement, focus behavior, headless slots, and composition boundaries.
- [Sidebar AI context](./sidebar/llms.txt): Deterministic Sidebar shell and trigger generation rules.
- [Menu documentation](./menu/README.md): Inline and popup commands, trigger directive, keyboard behavior, Overlay positioning, and headless slots.
- [Menu AI context](./menu/llms.txt): Deterministic flat command menu generation rules.
- [Popover documentation](./popover/README.md): Arbitrary content, top-layer positioning, dismissal, focus, class slots, and SSR.
- [Popover AI context](./popover/llms.txt): Deterministic non-modal Popover generation rules.

## APIs

- [Localization documentation](./i18n/README.md): Locale providers, runtime Signals, fallback rules, and SSR behavior.
- [Localization AI context](./i18n/llms.txt): Deterministic locale configuration and override rules.
- [Color Mode documentation](./color-mode/README.md): Optional light/dark/system Signals, persistence, DOM contract, Tailwind integration, and SSR first-paint guidance.
- [Color Mode AI context](./color-mode/llms.txt): Deterministic generation rules for color-mode control.
- [Message documentation](./message/README.md): Inline feedback component plus the headless Signal store, providers, channels, references, and renderer contract.
- [Message AI context](./message/llms.txt): Deterministic rules for inline Message and application notifications.
- [MeterGroup documentation](./meter-group/README.md): Multiple scalar measurements, shared ranges, accessibility, layout, and headless styling.
- [MeterGroup AI context](./meter-group/llms.txt): Deterministic generation rules for measurement composition.
- [Overlay documentation](./overlay/README.md): Shared native-first floating UI positioning.
- [Overlay AI context](./overlay/llms.txt): Low-level placement and lifecycle rules.

## Themes

- [Neutral theme](./themes/neutral.css): Stable light/dark semantic and component token values.
- [Tailwind v4 bridge](./themes/tailwind.css): Optional `primary-*` and `surface-*` utility namespaces.
- [Experimental Glass theme](./themes/experimental/glass.css): Optional Glass token values scoped to `data-neural-theme="glass"`.
- [Experimental Mist theme](./themes/experimental/mist.css): Calm translucent token values scoped to `data-neural-theme="mist"`.
- [Experimental Futuristic theme](./themes/experimental/futuristic.css): Optional Futuristic token values scoped to `data-neural-theme="futuristic"`.

## Optional

- [Package README](./README.md): Human-oriented overview, setup, and workspace commands.
- [llms.txt specification](https://llmstxt.org/): Format used by these AI context files.

Editor collaboration: pass an application-owned `Y.Doc` through
`NeuralEditorCollaborationConfig`. NeuralNg does not create providers, rooms,
tokens, or persistence. Wait for initial provider sync before mounting/seed, use
awareness only for ephemeral presence, and let Collaboration own undo/redo.
Comments, suggestion-mode text changes, and JSON snapshots are beta review
primitives; enforce permissions and durable history in application/backend code.
